tw-mi-higgins-lake-flynn-island-hermit-c.st: A second island dweller explains the 'rich hermit' tale: in 1891 Newton Phelps, a Grand Rapids heir with a $25,000 trust, lived on a low Higgins Lake island in a $1,200 house, was judged slightly demented, and kept his money under his pillow with two revolvers and a dirk; the papers do not name the island. Pritchard, the later hermit, was a poor county charge.
tw-mi-higgins-lake-flynn-island-hermit-c.t: A sweep of papers for 1890-1940 found no treasure story; the cache legend is a later blend of the rich Phelps (1891) and the poor Pritchard (1902).

set.tovw: Late secondary telling, disputed by a descendant; period papers show a rich 1891 islander and a pauper 1902 hermit, no cache
